target_moa.text: Insulin degludec is a long-acting basal human insulin analog whose primary activity is regulation of glucose metabolism; it lowers blood glucose by stimulating peripheral glucose uptake (skeletal muscle and fat) and inhibiting hepatic glucose production, and it forms multi-hexamers on subcutaneous injection to produce a long, flat glucose-lowering effect

citations.quote: The primary activity of insulin, including TRESIBA, is regulation of glucose metabolism. Insulin and its analogs lower blood glucose by stimulating peripheral glucose uptake, especially by skeletal muscle and fat, and by inhibiting hepatic glucose production. Insulin also inhibits lipolysis and proteolysis, and enhances protein synthesis. TRESIBA forms multi-hexamers when injected into the subcuta

Insulin degludec is a new, long-acting, insulin dosed according to an individual's metabolic needs and administered subcutaneously once daily to cover background (i.e., basal) insulin requirements in patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

TRESIBA (insulin degludec injection) is a long-acting basal human insulin analog for subcutaneous injection. Insulin degludec is produced by a process that includes expression of recombinant DNA in *Saccharomyces cerevisiae* followed by chemical modification.

key_safety.text: Hypoglycemia is the most common adverse reaction and may be life-threatening. Other common adverse reactions include allergic reactions, injection site reactions, lipodystrophy, pruritus, rash, edema and weight gain. Among non-hypoglycemia adverse reactions occurring in ≥5% of patients, nasopharyngitis had the highest rate in both populations: 23.9% in type 1 diabetes and 12.9% in type 2 diabetes. A signal of serious cardiovascular risk was also identified.

summary.text: TRESIBA was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA received September 29, 2011. Approval was refused on the first cycle via a Complete Response Letter dated 8 February 2013 (manufacturing deficiencies plus a cardiovascular safety signal). After an End-of-Review meeting, the sponsor filed a Class 2 resubmission on 26 March 2015 with reassuring interim results from the dedicated DEVOTE cardiovascular outcomes trial, leading to approval on September 25, 2015; FDA additionally required completion of the DEVOTE CVOT as a post-marketing requirement (PMR 2954-2).
